So it's possible to automate, but we'll have to investigate/think some more about how useful the suggestions actually are... Definitely not to be trusted blindly.
Yeah, thinking about it more, knowing which definitions to bash through is rarely that helpful... We really want #defeq_abuse to be identifying for you the non-normalized instances.

It looks like the fix here is to correct RestrictScalars.module, whose definition abuses RestrictScalars R S M := M.

We can do that hackily, with fast_instance%, but then you start getting sucked into adding fast_instance% also on RestrictScalars.algebra, and then Module.complexToReal and Algebra.complexToReal and ...
Maybe it is better to actually define RestrictScalars.module by explicit transport of structure along an equivalence RestrictScalars R S M \equiv M`, but this gets painful fast.

I guess what I would like is:

  1. #defeq_abuse at the examples above says "hey, RestrictScalara.module is leaky"
  2. We mechanically apply the band-aid fast_instance% there
  3. This causes more breakages downstream, but critically they are all fixable by adding more set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparancy false (despite the fact we're trying to reduce these!)
  4. However after we've repaired the actual failures, #defeq_abuse at those breakages successfully tell us about other instances that need repair, and we keep pushing the set_options later.
#36087

I'm not convinced this is the right solution. We shouldn't be making things like algebraMap implicit_reducible until we've actually fixed all the leaky instances built using inferInstanceAs (or plain defeq abuse!) in the vicinity.

Right?

Well, I don't think that RestrictScalars is really fixable, its design appears to be entirely based on defeq abuse. This is why that PR defines non-instance helpers that don't use RestrictScalars and moves towards using those. Given Algebra.algebraMap can already be normalized at implicit reducibility, I don't think having algebraMap not be makes much sense.
We can make RestrictScalars a one field structure if we want!
Are we sure that RestrictScalars is implicated here? Does bypassing it in this definition make the problem go away? (my guess would be not)

Looking at Matthew's PR, I think the changes to RestrictScalars (i.e., to avoid it in places where the user doesn't want the type synonmy at all) are very reasonable, and the changes to algebraMap suggest we are in trouble

The algebraMap changes seem to lead to one of the following conclusions:

  • Bundled maps should never be typeclass fields; these should instead be raw functions provided directly, with separate proofs that they satisfy the required properties.
  • All bundled maps should be instance-reducible to their unbundled forms.
  • There should be a way of tagging troublesome typeclass fields along the lines of attribute [unify_with_reducibility default] Algebra.toRingHom
